cues: After harvest, curved tropical fruit is sorted by ripeness before its bunches travel to neighborhood markets.
A cook removes the thick skin, slices the sweet flesh, and folds it into a chilled fruit salad.
At a smoothie bar, ripe pieces are blended with yogurt until the drink turns creamy and fragrant.
Workers cut mature bunches from tall plants, then rinse and pack the fruit for export.
The peeled fruit browns quickly after cutting, so cooks add citrus juice before serving it raw.
A dessert maker mashes soft golden flesh into batter, adding moisture to a loaf without extra oil.
For a quick snack, someone peels a ripe piece and eats its soft, sweet center by hand.
In warm climates, growers protect developing fruit from bruising and harvest it while the flesh remains firm.
